modern: Just as those who try to stand in your way when you are going forward according to right reason will not be able to turn you aside from your proper action, so do not let them drive you from your kindly feelings towards them either; but be on your guard equally in both matters, not only in steady judgement and action, but also in gentleness towards those who try to stop or otherwise trouble you. For this too is a weakness, to be irritated with them, just as it is to be turned from your course of action and to give way through fear; for both are equally deserters from their post—the man who does it through fear, and the man who is estranged from one who is by nature his kinsman and friend.
original: As those who try to stand in thy way when thou art proceeding according to right reason will not be able to turn thee aside from thy proper action, so neither let them drive thee from thy benevolent feelings toward them, but be on thy guard equally in both matters, not only in the matter of steady judgment and action, but also in the matter of gentleness to those who try to hinder or otherwise trouble thee. For this also is a weakness, to be vexed at them, as well as to be diverted from thy course of action and to give way through fear; for both are equally deserters from their post,—the man who does it through fear, and the man who is alienated from him who is by nature a kinsman and a friend.
